## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sutasomacariya* ("The Conduct of Sutasoma", Cp 32) is a canonical verse narrative belonging to the *Cariyāpiṭaka* section of the late Pali Sutta Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The text recounts the bodhisatta's conduct in past lives as King Sutasoma, exemplifying the perfection of virtues leading to awakening within the present aeon (*kappa*) [Bareau, Récits canoniques]. In modern scholarship, André Bareau identifies and enumerates it as the thirty-second story (*Sutasoma-Cariyam*) in his study of canonical *Cariyāpiṭaka* narratives and their relation to the Pali Jātakas [Bareau, Récits canoniques]. An English translation entitled *The Conduct of Sutasoma* has been produced by Bhikkhu Sujato, with translations into two other modern languages also recorded [SuttaCentral].

In terms of parallels and text reuse, SuttaCentral identifies no external parallels in Chinese Āgama, Sanskrit, or Tibetan collections [SuttaCentral]. Automated alignment via DharmaNexus likewise reports no cross-language matches meeting significance thresholds [DharmaNexus]. Within Pali literature, DharmaNexus identifies 13 matching segments (comprising 711 characters in total) shared exclusively with its traditional commentary, the *Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā* (Atk S0512a), with the longest continuous correspondence occurring between §3.3–4.2 of the root text and §1736_2–1737_0 of the commentary [DharmaNexus].
